full_judgment:
6. Mr Khandker Khaliqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the Rule petitioner submits that from the very filing of the suit the late defendant No. 11 was one of the contesting defendant of the suit. He preferred the title appeal against the judgment of the trial Court and thereafter moved to the High Court Division filing Civil Revision No. 3108 of 2003 and during pendency of the said Civil Revision in the High Court Division the said Abdus Samad died. Thereafter his heirs took also interest in the Civil Revision but ultimately the Rule in the Civil Revision was discharged and though the heirs of Abdus Samad un-successfully moved to the Appellate Division but they had no knowledge about the movement of the suit in the trial Court. The plaintiff substituted the heirs of Abdus Samad in the record of the trial Court on 31-5-2017. Thereafter on the following month the heirs of Abdus Samad got the notice about the substitution and about the suit and they making query came to know that in their absence amendment petition was allowed changing the schedule of the plaint. Thereafter they filed the Civil Revision in the Court of District Judge, Sylhet followed by an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act explaining the cause and reason as to why the revision could not be filed within the shortest possible time. 

 12. Having gone through the records and on considering the 'oral submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties it appears that the submissions of the learned Advocates relating to the facts of the case and its development from the date of filing are almost consistent with the materials on record. The only question before me needs to be considered or addressed whether the learned District Judge was justified in rejecting the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act and also in not admitting the Civil Revision. 

 14. In the law of limitation there is no prescribe time limit for filing a Civil Revision either in the Court of District Judge or High Court Division but normally the time limit for filing the appeal in the Civil jurisdiction is maintained and considered for filing of the Civil Revision and by this time some important decision has been given by the Appellate Division as to how the limitation matter of the Civil Revision should be guided. 

 15. In the case of Deputy Commissioner vs Kobad Ali 39 DLR (AD) 205 the Appellate Division held that there is a long standing practice being followed since the days of Dhaka High Court that a revisional application is to be filed within the period of ninety days, prescribed by law for an appeal, and that the High Court Division may in its discretion entertain an application beyond that period in a suitable case where there is no negligence or 'aches on the part of the petitioner and this is a long standing practice, otherwise sound and reasonable, and it does not call for any departure. Though the above decision came out in a case of a High Court Division but the principle is applicable for 'the District Judge also for consideration the limitation matter of a Civil Revision. 

 16. On going through the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act as have been filed in the Court of District Judge it appears that the petitioners explained categorically as to why they could not file an application within the shortest possible time from the date of impugned order. In the petition it has been articulated that the present petitioners as heirs of original defendant No. 11 received the summons of the suit on 7-6-2017, thereafter they appearing in the suit on 09-7-2017 came to know about the said amendment dated 27-4-2016 and they taking the certified copy of the impugned order preferred Civil Revisional application on 7-11-2017, so I find that the delay has been explained satisfactorily in the application for condonation of delay but form the order of the District Judge it is difficult to hold that he at all considered the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act judiciously.
